question: which mechanisms make up the instructions per key by which sync_strmap_scan (the string batch cursor, METHODOLOGY section 33.11) exceeds sync_strmap_scan_locked after A3; the input of section 33.12
metric: Callgrind retired instructions (Ir), exact integers, no interval (AGENTS.md section 8.4)

provenance.host: development box, 72-core x86_64 (NOT the reference host; no bench lock taken, no wall-clock claim is made from this artifact)
provenance.source: git archive 93913eca into a scratch tree plus one scratch crate, `scanprof` (source under `harness.source`), added to the workspace members. The engine is unmodified. The crate is NOT committed
provenance.build_profile: bench profile (lto = thin, codegen-units = 1, as CI) plus CARGO_PROFILE_BENCH_DEBUG=1 for annotation
provenance.not_the_reference_host: measured on a development box; Callgrind counts are deterministic, so AGENTS.md section 8.17's load-snapshot requirement does not apply and none was taken
provenance.provenance_gate: the file name is outside scripts/check_bench_provenance.py's ARTIFACT_GLOBS, as callgrind_929_bytes_price_0b08dd5b.json is: a deterministic Ir artifact has no rounds, no estimator and no interval

harness.relation_to_ci: the two scan functions are the bodies of `sync_strmap_scan` and `sync_strmap_scan_locked` in crates/expanse/benches/instructions.rs, over the same key generator (`path_keys`, 50,000 keys, same seed); collection is toggled on the scan function only, as iai-callgrind measures the benchmark function only
harness.harness_heap: each profile carries about 3.6 M Ir of glibc malloc_consolidate and unlink_chunk, run inside the scan's first allocation because of the heap state this harness's setup leaves. It is the same in both arms and is not engine work; it is reported as the group `harness_heap` and excluded from every per-key figure. With it excluded the per-key totals agree with CI run 41335458877 (commit 86690edf, the same engine code) within 1%: see `ci_cross_check`

groups.description: each (source file, symbol) row is assigned to one group; a symbol's rows are split by the source file its inlined bodies come from. Rule, in order: glibc malloc rows -> harness_heap; locked arm: strmap::push_* -> key_build, scanprof::* -> consumer, the rest (Walk::next, sibling, descend_from and what they inline) -> walk; cursor arm: StrBatch::push and __memcpy_* -> key_copy, scanprof::* -> consumer, rows from sync_nav.rs or core sync/atomic.rs -> validation, the rest (drain_in, the inlined SyncStrMapCursor::current with scan_validated and fill_scan_batch, decode_value) -> drain_pass_handoff
groups.implementation: the grouping is recomputed from `profiles.*.rows` by scripts/str_cursor_bounds.py (`str_cursor_profile_groups`), whose self-test checks it against `profiles.*.groups_ir`
